note: The single reviewed exception mechanism for verify-expungement-plain-language-values. It does not excuse a parity failure. Each record is APPLIED to the origin/main baseline to produce the exact expected shape, and the verifier's existing strict comparison then runs unchanged against that. Anything outside the recorded delta is still a failure, because the expected result is fully specified rather than partially waived. Unknown keys are rejected and no field accepts a wildcard, a prefix or a glob, so widening scope requires changing the schema and its tests, not editing a list.

proofRevisions.author: Roger Roman
proofRevisions.reason: Chain origin under the 2026-08-29 authorization, not a revision of 74624c8464e40e02c272b967ebeba42452681d163ea4be6d013af01778b7759d. One line WAS removed from the previous proof, and that is precisely why this is a new authorization rather than a revision: the mechanism refuses a revision that removes anything, and it is right to. The removed line was assert.doesNotThrow(() => assertCheckoutAllowed(protectedVerification.snapshot)) against a Mississippi route. Once Grade-A authority became the checkout gate, that assertion could only pass if Mississippi held a fulfillment record, and Mississippi is a retired legacy generator that must never hold one. It is replaced by assert.throws requiring the refusal /cannot prove it delivers the packet it promises/, so the proof now proves the denial and pins its reason by message. History this chain replaces: 6bb400d605977d49d8410fd27390b6a4501db78d on 2026-08-27 added 82 lines and removed none, strengthening the proof to preserve protected fact sources; that work is still in the file and is not undone here. Authorized by Roger Roman on 2026-08-29, byte-exact per docs/rcap/grade-a/lane-j/patches/blocker-5-mississippi-proof-proposed.diff at Lane J commit 7b37de68679941c1efdf74e889ef5b9014bdef6b, repository non-production only. It creates no Mississippi fulfillment record, opens no checkout, and reaches no legal conclusion.

proofRevisions.author: Roger Roman
proofRevisions.reason: Recorded after the fact. Commit b680a4e4d ("Repair sponsored Mississippi Preview finalization") added 40 lines to the proof and removed none, and nothing re-recorded the move, so the suite began failing an approval nobody had withdrawn - the same way it did on 2026-08-27. Every added line is a key in the synthetic completePacketAnswers fixture: the Mississippi non-conviction route's required fact set had grown, and the proof's fixture had not, so the proof was exercising an incomplete matter. No assertion, branch or control was added, removed, weakened or reordered, and the fixture is synthetic data inside a verifier that never runs in production. This revision therefore re-pins the proof only. It does not touch priorSha256 or newSha256, which remain the exact public-profile-projection bytes this approval authorizes, and it changes nothing in the approval's scope or its doesNotAuthorize list: no screening question, evaluator, date or legal behaviour is authorized differently than it was on 2026-08-26.

authorization.statement: Roger Roman and the LegalEase legal team approve the exact current Maryland pardon screening behavior, the exact LD-MD-03 police-record eight-year arrest-date filing deadline, and the exact file bytes pinned by this record. Approval remains limited to Maryland: pardon_signed_date retains its date_or_unknown type, timing_and_completion placement and pardoned-conviction pathway, while arrest_date is collected as the prepay deadline anchor for the police-record route. It preserves route-relevant uncertainty, ignores only unrelated unknown facts, and does not authorize any other screening mutation. No existing question may be removed, renamed, reordered or substantively changed. This is not a generic parity bypass or wildcard allowlist, and it authorizes no migration, deployment, worker publication, staging change, production change or nationwide launch.

supersededSha256.reason: Public-witness reachability corrections to the shared evaluator: the timing gate now only names anchor questions the public profile actually publishes and falls back to the timing bucket, and the timing-gate and compiled-route failure branches now report the pathway they had already resolved instead of dropping it. Neither touches the Maryland pardon route this delta approves — no question is added, removed, renamed, reordered or retyped, no eligibility rule changes, and the ten-year filing period under Crim. Proc. 10-105(c)(4) is evaluated exactly as approved.

The evaluator's idea of today is now the authoritative clock in production. RCAP_EVALUATOR_TODAY pins it for the deterministic 284-pathway witness replay and is refused when NODE_ENV is production, where honouring it would compute every waiting period against a frozen day. This delta approves the Maryland pardon question, its placement and the ten-year filing period under Crim. Proc. 10-105(c)(4); none of that changes. No question is added, removed, renamed, reordered or retyped, and no eligibility rule moves. What changes is which clock the deadline is measured against outside tests, which is the clock the approval always assumed.

The production test no longer depends on the spelling of an environment variable. It matched NODE_ENV === "production" exactly, so Production, PRODUCTION and prod all bypassed it and froze the evaluator's clock; it now matches any prod-prefixed NODE_ENV in any case and consults VERCEL_ENV as well, because a deployment can set that without NODE_ENV agreeing. This delta approves the Maryland pardon question, its placement and the ten-year filing period under Crim. Proc. 10-105(c)(4); none of that changes. No question is added, removed, renamed, reordered or retyped, and no eligibility rule moves.

The final captain integrates route-scoped ambiguity for California, exact Corrections A anchors and Mississippi clocks, concrete service classifications for all thirty-six Corrections A routes, and legal-contract authority over stale packet-plan labels. Roger Roman and the LegalEase legal team expressly approve the Maryland pardon behavior over the final bytes. The Maryland question, placement, pathway, missing-date outcome and ten-year filing deadline remain unchanged and are independently verifier-proven.

The Maryland profile now consumes LD-MD-03 instead of remaining exempt from legal-contract binding. The change replaces the route's unrelated shared waiting statements with the approved § 10-103 eight-year filing-deadline statement, records the agency-application output, and binds arrest_date. The pardon question, pathway, placement, counts and ten-year pardon deadline remain unchanged.

The evaluator now consumes LD-MD-03 as an approved Maryland agency application, asks for the exact arrest_date anchor, permits filings through the exact eight-year boundary, and returns the statute-specific ineligibility result after the deadline. The Maryland pardon behavior and every unrelated route remain independently verifier-proven.

The final evaluator bytes move nine Pennsylvania routes from a stale hold set into the exact approved-release guidance set and add the route-specific approved guidance reason. Roger Roman and the LegalEase legal team approve those exact Pennsylvania bytes while expressly retaining the previously approved Maryland pardon and LD-MD-03 behavior. The Maryland question, pathway, placement, counts, missing-date result, ten-year pardon deadline, eight-year police-record maximum window, and unrelated-mutation detection remain unchanged and independently verifier-proven.

Commit 3716eba4 (2026-08-27, 'fix(rcap): keep exact route dates postpay') added pardon_signed_date and arrest_date to questionLifecycle.exactPacketFactIds, which moves both out of anonymous screening and into the authenticated packet-information step. The signed statement is unaffected and is proven still to hold: arrest_date remains the prepay deadline anchor, collected after the claim and before checkout, and the eight-year window is still a maximum filing deadline that permits the exact boundary and bars a later request. Before this commit the exact arrest date was asked of an anonymous person, which the free-screening boundary does not permit; the re-pin records a correction, not a departure.

Shared evaluator changes for the national legal decision report: the Missouri 311.326 clock now runs twenty-two years from a date of birth collected after authentication rather than from an unpublished anchor, the controlling route contract decides route kind where an adjudication applies, a recorded route-presentation conflict holds its own route, and a route the contract identifies but cannot yet deliver reports that instead of a ready packet. None of it touches Maryland: no Maryland question is added, removed, renamed, reordered or retyped, no Maryland eligibility rule changes, and both Maryland deadlines are re-proven end to end over these bytes.

Projection changes for the same report: a route contract's packetReleasePreconditions now publish their facts as post-claim packet fields, because a fact deliberately kept out of screening previously had no publication path at all, and Missouri's exact birth-date question was replaced by an approximate age threshold. Maryland is untouched by both. This continues the chain after the 2026-08-26 runtime re-authorization rather than editing that authorization's newSha256, which would put a signature on bytes nobody signed for.

Mississippi § 99-15-59 was proven to generate a status summary rather than a filing, so the evaluator now holds it at needs_review with no payment; a route recorded in data/rcap-ledger/packet-correction-required.json is closed at the evaluator as well as at the packet route resolver, because closing only the resolver stops the sale and still reports a ready packet. Maryland is untouched: no Maryland question, rule or deadline changes, and both Maryland deadlines are re-proven end to end over these bytes.

The seven per-route ratification Sets became projections of data/record-clearing/legal-decisions/route-ratification-registry.json. The repository carried two editable records of the same legal fact and they disagreed; the registry is now the authority and the evaluator filters it. The projected membership is identical to the literals it replaced, set for set — ratified 80, corrected 4, hard-gate 37, held 31, approved-release 9, unsupported 24, caution-override 2, with the same route keys in each. So no route's ratification changed and Maryland's pardon route is ratified exactly as before. What changed is where the list is stored. This delta approves the Maryland pardon question, its placement and the ten-year filing period under Crim. Proc. 10-105(c)(4); none of that moves.

Each pathway's lawrenceRatification block is now written from the ratification registry rather than carried as an independently editable copy. That field is listed in INTERNAL_LEAK_MARKERS in src/lib/content/state-resources.ts: it must never reach the public projection, and it does not. It cannot add, remove, rename, reorder or retype a question, cannot move an eligibility rule, and cannot change the ten-year filing period under Crim. Proc. 10-105(c)(4). Maryland's pardon route keeps the same ratified status it had. The bytes moved for a reason outside what this approval covers, which is what a re-pin is for; the approval is not rehashed and nobody's name is put on bytes they did not see.

Commit 78e79be41 (2026-09-05, 'Give five proven families a runtime route identity of their own') added ten lines to the compiled Maryland profile and changed nothing else in it. The whole delta is one entry appended to pathways[2].legalAuthority.serviceBranches on police-record-expungement-when-no-charge-was-filed-under-10-103, recording the branch identity LD-MD-03 names for that route's AUTOMATIC STATUS/CORRECTION GUIDANCE treatment. It carries no selector and a null packet family, so it opens no route, selects no disposition and invents no predicate; it records a requirement the branch-identity and packet-factory lanes still owe. This delta approves the pardon_signed_date question on pardoned-conviction-expungement-under-crim-proc-10-105-a-8, its placement in timing_and_completion, the 35 -> 36 participant-facing count and the ten-year filing period under Crim. Proc. 10-105(c)(4). None of that is touched: no question is added, removed, renamed, reordered or retyped, no evaluator rule moves, and no date behaviour changes. A different pathway gained a declarative legal-authority record, and the approved shape is unchanged - which the strict parity comparison this file feeds re-proves against the new bytes on every run.

Commits 27eec639c and ae60d7824 (2026-09-19, GA-5-NV) added three Nevada questions (nv_176a_excluded_charge_class, nv_176a_charge_class, nv_176a_disposition_class) and 658bd4371 (2026-09-20) added one South Dakota question (sd_sis_record_correction_stage) to the aggregate. The Maryland projection inside the aggregate is canonically identical before and after (18 questions, same order, same stages), so the approved MD pardon behaviour holds over the new bytes; the NV and SD additions are covered by their own delta records, not by this approval. No Maryland question is added, removed, renamed, reordered or retyped and no Maryland date behaviour changes.

Commits 27eec639c and ae60d7824 (2026-09-19, GA-5-NV) moved the shared evaluator: the NRS 176A.245/.265/.295 subsection 2 branch trigger, the subsection 3 bar (NRS 200.508 / 200.5099), Spanish resolution of the four Nevada engine reason texts and required-fact completeness for the Nevada probation-sealing family.
